- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day forecast horizon, especially for the first 5–10 days.
- Model overestimates prices after sharp upward spikes in the history (e.g., after 85+ values), often overshooting by 2–5% and failing to correct.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: tends to forecast prices back toward historical averages too aggressively, especially after prolonged high or low periods.
- Forecast lags the true price movement by 1–3 days, particularly in the first 10 days of the forecast window.
- Model underreacts to recent downward trends in history, often failing to anticipate sharp drops in the next 5–7 days.
- Model overreacts to recent upward trends, especially when history includes a spike followed by a dip — forecasts often peak too early and then drop too slowly.
- Model tends to underestimate the magnitude of price corrections after spikes, especially in the 10–15 day window.
- Model shows persistent bias toward lower prices in the final 5–7 days of the forecast, even when history shows upward momentum.
